prompt:
Create a complete 10-level Android mobile game named 'Arrow Flow: Crash Course' featuring a clean, modern UI with a dynamic dark/light theme and a cosmic blue/orange accent. The game must be structured across multiple Java/Kotlin component files (at least 15, including Activities, Fragments, Custom Views, and Game Logic classes) and XML layouts. The core gameplay involves managing a chaotic field of arrows on a grid.
​Game Mechanics:
​Levels & Complexity: Implement 10 progressive levels. Each level starts with a randomized, scattered arrangement of arrows on the playfield. The number of arrows must increase with each level (e.g., Level 1: 10 arrows, Level 10: 50+ arrows).
​Arrow Properties: Each arrow has a specific direction (Up, Down, Left, Right). Some arrows have a clear path, while others are positioned to collide head-on with another arrow.
​Interaction: The player must identify arrows that have a clear forward path (no obstacles immediately in front) and "flick" or "tap" them with their finger.
​Animation & Logic: When tapped, the arrow must animate smoothly, moving across the screen in its direction until it either goes off the playfield boundary or crashes into another arrow.
​Collision & Crashing: If two moving arrows collide (head-on or side-swipe), a visual "CRASH" animation/particle effect must play, and the level must fail (Game Over).
​Score & Progress: If an arrow successfully exits the screen, the player gains points (based on speed and distance). The level is won when all arrows that can move have successfully exited. An arrow that crashes prevents level completion.
​Technical Requirements:
​Use core Android View classes or a lightweight 2D graphics canvas for the game grid.
​Implement touch event listeners for detecting arrow flicks/taps.
​Create smooth object-oriented animations (ObjectAnimator or ValueAnimator) for arrow movement.
​Establish a game loop/logic to check for arrow positions, collisions, and exit conditions after each move.
​Include a Score Manager and Level Completion logic to unlock the next level.
​UI Elements:
​A main dashboard showing the current level, score, and a 'Restart Level' button.
​A level-complete screen with stats and a 'Next Level' button.
​Distinct visual designs for moving arrows, crashed arrows, and the playfield grid."*
